html:
In 1783 the Al Khalifa, a clan of the Bani Utbah tribe based at Zubarah in Qatar, took Bahrain from rulers who held it for Persia. The family has ruled Bahrain ever since.

The Utub had come down from central Arabia in the early 1700s and settled in Kuwait and on the Qatar coast, where they grew rich on pearls and trade. Taking Bahrain gave them the richest pearl banks of the Gulf.

Persia claimed the islands for long after, and Iran only dropped the claim around independence in 1971. The ruling family is Sunni, while most Bahrainis are Shia, a divide that shaped the island's politics up to the uprising of 2011.
